departments.name: Creative Direction
departments.mission: Own the creative vision: what the game is, why it deserves to exist, and the identity every other department builds against.
capabilities: creative pillars and non-negotiable design values
creative arbitration with the Studio Director

deliverables.name: Concept Brief
acceptance: A one-sentence hook and three named creative pillars
Genre, subgenre, dimension (2D/2.5D/3D/hybrid) and target platforms stated
At least three reference works with what to borrow and what to avoid
One testable differentiator that a competitor could not claim unchanged

deliverables.name: Art Direction Bible
acceptance: Palette, lighting mood and material language given as concrete values
Silhouette and shape-language rules a modeller can follow
Do and do-not lists, each traceable to a creative pillar
Platform-aware fidelity tiers (hero, standard, low) defined

deliverables.name: Creative Sign-off
acceptance: Every pillar checked against a built and playable version with evidence
Deviations either fixed or recorded as an accepted trade-off in the decision log

inputs: research and tech radar from D41
gates: No production work starts before the concept brief is approved
Art direction changes after prototype require a decision record

departments.name: Game Design
departments.mission: Turn the creative vision into systems, loops and numbers that can be implemented, tuned and tested.

deliverables.name: Game Design Document
acceptance: Core loop described as a cycle with a stated time to first reward
Every mechanic has inputs, rules, failure states and feedback
Progression and difficulty described with actual numbers and ranges
An explicit out-of-scope list signed by the Studio Director

deliverables.name: Balance and Tuning Plan
acceptance: Tuning tables or curves with base values and permitted ranges
Economy or progression faucets and sinks named and scoped
Every tuned value has a telemetry hook or a deterministic test

deliverables.name: Tuning Report
acceptance: Measured playtest or simulation data attached, not opinion
Each change traced to data or a decision record

inputs: concept brief and art direction from D01
telemetry and bug data from D33
gates: A mechanic with no failure state or no feedback is rejected
Balance claims without numbers or evidence are rejected

departments.name: World Building
departments.mission: Design the world the game happens in: geography, biomes, settlements, landmarks, infrastructure and lore that make the place feel real.

deliverables.name: World Bible
acceptance: Regions and biomes listed with gameplay purpose for each
Landmark and point-of-interest budget stated in numbers
World history and faction context that explains the current state
Scale and traversal times consistent with the movement budget

deliverables.name: World Layout and Biome Table
acceptance: Playable-space map or schematic with coordinates or grid
Per-biome palette, prop set and density targets
Hand-authored versus generated areas explicitly divided

deliverables.name: World Consistency Review
acceptance: Named locations in the build match the world bible or the bible is updated
Traversal times measured in the build against the stated budget

gates: A world area with no gameplay or narrative purpose is rejected
Lore that contradicts an approved spec requires a decision record

departments.name: Narrative and Storytelling
departments.mission: Give the game a story worth playing through: arcs, characters, quests, dialogue, factions and the way the world tells its own story.

deliverables.name: Story Arc and Character Bible
acceptance: Three-act or equivalent structure with act goals and turn points
Every named character has motivation, conflict and arc
Branching points listed with their consequences and cost
Word-count and voice-line budget stated

deliverables.name: Quest and Dialogue Set
acceptance: Quests have objectives, failure, rewards and preconditions
Dialogue is scripted with speaker, trigger and fallback lines
Every branch reachable in a build and verified once

deliverables.name: Narrative Review
acceptance: No unreachable or dead-end narrative content in the build
Tone and terminology consistent with the world bible

gates: Dialogue that cannot be triggered in a build is rejected
Every named character must exist in the shared knowledge base

departments.name: User Experience and Interface
departments.mission: Make the game legible and operable on every target device, including for players using accessibility features.

deliverables.name: UX Flows and Screen Inventory
acceptance: Every screen listed with entry points, states and exit paths
HUD information hierarchy prioritised with a rationale
Input schemes for every declared platform described
Accessibility options enumerated with what they change

deliverables.name: Interface Specification
acceptance: Components specified with sizes, spacing, states and text limits
Safe-area and resolution rules including mobile notches
Animation and transition timings in milliseconds

deliverables.name: Interface Review
acceptance: Every screen reachable and operable on each declared platform
Text overflow, focus order and touch target sizes verified in the build
Contrast and readability checked against the art direction

gates: A screen without a failure or empty state is rejected
Touch targets below 44 px on mobile are rejected
